segments.title: Members of the Holmes Band of Lutcher photo
segments.summary: Joseph and the interviewers identify players in a photo of the Holmes Band: the one-handed bass drummer John Porter, Floyd Jackson, Davy Jones, Henry Sawyer, Dennis Harris, and cornetists Professor Holmes and Joe Poehler.

segments.title: Davy Jones moves from snare drum to saxophone
segments.summary: Jones left snare drum, took up a saxophone after a stay in Chicago; Bill Russell relays that Jones was credited with teaching local players chords.

segments.title: Professor Anthony Holmes teaches Joseph and gets him a saxophone
segments.summary: Joseph says Professor Anthony Holmes taught him, moved him from bass to a saxophone he bought, and he was playing in the band within three weeks.

segments.title: Recording date and Floyd Jackson, who stayed in the country
segments.summary: Allen states the date, January 18, 1962, and the interviewers; Floyd Jackson is described as a good musician who never played in the city and is still living.

segments.title: Playing in the country band at Leclerc after 1913; reading and playing by head
segments.summary: Joseph returned to Leclerc in 1913 and played with the Holmes men, the only band there; they all read music and played by ear.

segments.title: When the Holmes photo was taken and the band's city visits
segments.summary: Joseph dates the picture about 1901; the band came to New Orleans for carnival, playing parades and dances.

segments.title: History of the banjo and the five- and six-string banjos
segments.summary: Joseph recalls the three-string banjo first, then guitar, then six- and four-string banjos; the men look at an old five-string banjo and mandolin and talk about a trip to Bridge City.

segments.title: Identifying the players in the Ory band picture and its tonk style
segments.summary: Joseph names Foster on bass, Stone on guitar and Chiff's brother, and says the Ory band played blues and tonk music while Holmes's reading men played differently.

segments.title: Drum pedal and use of Derby mutes in the picture
segments.summary: The men examine the crowfoot pedal and what is in the grass by Ory's foot, and Joseph says the only mute used then was the derby.

segments.title: Holmes taught Joseph his first notes
segments.summary: Joseph says that from across the river Holmes came to his home band and taught him clarinet, the first man to teach him a note.

segments.title: Kid Ory and others playing at Joseph's dance place
segments.summary: Ory played occasionally for the dances at Joseph's place across from his barbershop; Oliver, Ben and Bunk did too.

segments.title: The 12-string guitar and the unnamed violinist in the Ory band
segments.summary: Stone is dead; the violinist, whose sons played trumpet and piano, still lives uptown but Joseph cannot recall his name.

segments.title: Violin talk and where the Ory photograph came from
segments.summary: Joseph on playing violin; the men study the photo's setting and Joseph says he got it from John Porter about five years earlier.

segments.title: The Ory band's instruments: drum set-up, valve trombone, first slide
segments.summary: Joseph and Allen discuss the dead drummer, bass drum with crowfoot pedal and side cymbal, homemade traps and hitting the rim instead of wood blocks. Ory's trombone was a valve trombone; Henry Sawyer was the first man Joseph saw with a slide.

segments.title: Joseph's age, birth year and his parents
segments.summary: Joseph was born in 1876 per his mother's Bible record; she died about nine years earlier, and his father was ten years old in slavery.

segments.title: Foster the bass player and his brother Dude
segments.summary: Foster is no relation to Pops Foster; he is Foster Lewis, Dude's brother, who played bass then trombone, even in church before he died.

segments.title: Trying to name the violin player; the bass drummer Rabbit
segments.summary: Eddie Summers arrives; the men identify the bass drummer as Rabbit and try to recall the violinist, settling on Raymond.

segments.title: Raymond Brown, Clifford Brown and the Mag Darcy band
segments.summary: Joseph names the violinist as Raymond Brown, also a trombonist, and lists players in the Mag Darcy band: Joe Harris, Tom Harris, Clifford Brown, Sammy Penn, Freddie Jones.

segments.title: Freddie Jones, Freddie Landry and other players
segments.summary: Allen asks about the clarinet and Freddie Jones; Joseph calls Freddie Landry one of the best drummers, living in Donaldsonville.

segments.title: Sullivan, Miney John and the drummer Bolegs
segments.summary: Joseph recalls Sullivan on clarinet, the trumpeter Miney John, his own trio with his brother at First and Liberty, and the drummer Bolegs who was refused Claven Williams's daughter.

segments.title: Plans to visit Floyd Jackson, the multi-instrumentalist
segments.summary: Joseph wants to take the interviewers to see Floyd Jackson, who played trumpet, organ, piano, trombone, bass violin and sousaphone.

segments.title: Return of the pictures and end of the tape
segments.summary: Russell gets Joseph's address to return the photographs; the interviewers thank him and end the tape.
